_meta.purpose: Real published figures for SLATE: credit-mark aging, holiday-let damage, mattress wear and removal, household moves and duty relief.
_meta.conventions: Each figure carries source URL, publisher, date (as published; null when the page shows none), sourceType ('primary' = the body that sets the rule or collected the data; 'secondary' = a reproduction or third-party guide), and confirmed (true = read on the fetched page this session; false = seen only in a search snippet or a reproduction and not checked against the original). A figure nobody publishes is null with a note. American spelling in the notes; quotations keep their original spelling.
_meta.method: Web search plus page fetches on 2026-09-30. Several PDFs (CFPB 2023 data point, Gross/Notowidigdo/Wang, Fed 2011 presentation) could not be text-extracted here; figures from those rely on the agency's HTML summary or a search snippet and are marked accordingly.

principle.claim: The older a derogatory mark, the less it weighs; a 5-year-old collection hurts much less than a 5-month-old one.
principle.quote: the older they are the less impact they are going to have on your FICO® score. For example, a collection that is 5 years old will hurt much less than a collection that is 5 months old.

principle.claim: Collections' impact lessens gradually as they age; paid collections are ignored by FICO 9 and FICO 10.
principle.quote: As with any derogatory information, when reported, its impact on a FICO Score will gradually lessen over time as they age off the credit report.  /  Collections reported as paid in full are disregarded by FICO® Score 9 and the FICO® Score 10 suite.

principle.claim: Payment history is 35% of the FICO score; older problems count less.
principle.quote: The older a credit problem, the less it counts toward your credit score.

principle.claim: A recent late payment can hurt more than several old ones; getting current before charge-off lets the score recover.
principle.quote: a recent late payment, could be more damaging to your score than a number of late payments that happened a long time ago.

principle.claim: Experian (US): a default's impact lessens over time and when it drops off 'you might see another minor increase'; no point figure given.
principle.quote: Like all negative information, the default will naturally drop off your credit file after a period of time, at which point you might see another minor increase in your scores.

principle.claim: Community observation only (not FICO's statement): single 30/60-day lates lose most of their weight around 2 years; 90+-day lates and collections keep most of it until they fall off at 7 years.
principle.note: User anecdote, explicitly because FICO keeps the aging curve proprietary. Useful as a shape, not a figure.

US.rule: Most negative information up to 7 years; civil judgments 7 years or the statute of limitations if longer; bankruptcies up to 10 years (myFICO: Chapter 13 7 years, Chapter 7 10 years). Collections run 7 years from the original delinquency date.
US.note: CFPB page seen via search snippet; the myFICO page was fetched.

UK.rule: A default stays 6 years from the default date whether or not it is paid (paying marks it 'satisfied'). A CCJ stays 6 years from the judgment date; paid in full within one calendar month it is not registered at all.
quotes: A default will stay on your credit file for six years from the date of default, regardless of whether you pay off the debt.
As your default ages, it may become less important to lenders.
A CCJ will stay on your credit report for six years from the date of the judgement.
If you pay the full amount within one calendar month of the CCJ being issued, it will not be recorded on the Register of Judgments, Orders and Fines.
UK.note: The ICO page, as fetched, treats a debt staying longer than six years from the original default as unlikely to be fair (e.g., when a sold debt is re-recorded); it does not itself state a blanket retention period.

IE.rule: Central Credit Register: information held 5 years after a loan is repaid, written off or discharged. If the borrower defaults and stops paying, the 5-year clock does not start and the loan keeps appearing.
quotes: the credit information is held on the Central Credit Register for a period 5 years after the loan is repaid, written off or discharged.
If you default on your loan agreement and cease making payments then the 5 year period will not start to run.
IE.publisher: Central Bank of Ireland (Central Credit Register)
IE.note: Covers loans of €500 or more under the Credit Reporting Act 2013 (per search snippet from CCPC; not fetched).

fico2011MortgageStudy.title: Research Looks at How Mortgage Delinquencies Affect Scores
fico2011MortgageStudy.publisher: FICO (Banking Analytics Blog), author Joanne Gaskin
primaryQuotes: The magnitude of FICO® Score impact is highly dependent on the starting score.
While a score may begin to improve sooner, it could take up to 7-10 years to fully recover, assuming all other obligations are paid as agreed.
In general, the higher starting score, the longer it takes for the score to fully recover.
There's no significant difference in score impact between short sale/deed-in-lieu/settlement and foreclosure.
fico2011MortgageStudy.tableNote: The table is an image on FICO's page and did not load. The rows below are assembled from reproductions: foreclosure/short-sale/bankruptcy rows fetched from bills.com and smartcredit.com (the latter a 2011-03-24 repost); the 30-day and 90-day rows from a search summary citing the same study. All reproductions agree where they overlap. Scores are the range after the event; profiles are hypothetical consumers with no other delinquencies.
fico2011MortgageStudy.relatedNote: A CBS MoneyWatch article (2011-04-28) on the same research names the starting scores as 650/720/780 rather than 680; every other reproduction and FICO's own post say 680.

scoreChangeWhenMarkFallsOff.event: Last medical collection removed from the report
scoreChangeWhenMarkFallsOff.figure: Average +25 points in the first quarter after removal; +21 for medical collections under $500, +32 for over $500.
scoreChangeWhenMarkFallsOff.note: Sample drawn from credit records 2012-2020 (per search snippet). The fetched page does not say whether removals were by aging-off, payment or deletion, so this is the nearest published measure of 'a collection disappears', not a clean 7-year aging-off measure.

scoreChangeWhenMarkFallsOff.event: Chapter 7 bankruptcy flag removed at 10 years (FCRA)
scoreChangeWhenMarkFallsOff.figure: About +15 points (616 to 631) in one study; about +10 points on a pre-removal mean of 596 in another; Chapter 13 flag removal about +12 points.
scoreChangeWhenMarkFallsOff.publisher: Gross, Notowidigdo & Wang (NBER working paper); Dobbie, Goldsmith-Pinkham, Mahoney & Song (NBER w22711 / Journal of Finance 2020)
scoreChangeWhenMarkFallsOff.date: 2018-01 (Gross et al. draft); 2020 (Dobbie et al., J. Finance)
scoreChangeWhenMarkFallsOff.note: Numbers from a search summary; the PDFs could not be text-extracted here. The NY Fed abstract (sr795) confirms Chapter 13 flag removal 'leads to a large increase in credit limits' but gives no point figure.

scoreChangeWhenMarkFallsOff.event: Paid vs unpaid medical collections (predictive accuracy, not a drop-off)
scoreChangeWhenMarkFallsOff.figure: Consumers whose collections were mostly medical performed like consumers scoring ~10 points higher; mostly paid medical collections, like ~20 points higher.

scoreChangeWhenMarkFallsOff.event: Non-medical collection, charge-off or repossession falling off at 7 years
scoreChangeWhenMarkFallsOff.note: No FICO, VantageScore, CFPB or Experian publication found that gives a point figure for this. Experian says only 'a minor increase'. FICO's position is that most of the decay happens before the drop-off.

frequency.note: The fetched page gave 2023-08-31; one secondary cites it as October 2024. The figure covers only large ($1,000+) reimbursed damage, not all claims.

claimCosts.figure: Average short-term rental sewer-backup claim in 2024: $18,000 (excluding lost rent). Paid examples: $130,000 guest-caused water damage (Newburyport, MA), $103,000 party damage, $50,000+ burst pipe.

airbnbProcess.deadline: Within 14 days of the responsible guest's checkout, file in the Resolution Center (help article 279); the Host Damage Protection terms say notify within 14 days of checkout and file payment requests within 30 days.
airbnbProcess.guestResponse: The guest has 24 hours to respond. If they don't respond, decline, or pay only part, the host can escalate under Host damage protection and Airbnb reviews it.
airbnbProcess.howGuestIsCharged: By booking, the guest authorizes Airbnb Payments to charge the booking payment method (or any method on file) for the Damage Report amount; Airbnb may also pursue the guest through collections or legal action.
airbnbProcess.cap: US$3 million (AirCover for Hosts, Host damage protection).
airbnbProcess.exclusions: Includes wear and tear/deterioration, acts of nature, mold, damage after checkout, linen stains except from pets or unauthorized guests.
airbnbProcess.note: 'Or before the next guest checks in, whichever comes first' appears in secondary host guides, not in the fetched Airbnb pages; treat 14 days after checkout as the rule. Terms of Service charging language is from a search snippet of article 2908.

vrboDeposit.rule: Amount set by the host; held as card on file, as an upfront refundable deposit, or replaced by purchased damage protection. Host has 14 days after checkout to claim; otherwise refunded after 14 days (plus up to 7 business days for the bank).

typicalAmount.note: Industry guide via search snippet; Vrbo publishes no typical amount. Same snippet: deposits of $5,000 or less are held as card on file, above that charged at booking — not confirmed on Vrbo's page.

sleepQualityVsAge.study: Jacobson, Boolani & Smith, 'Changes in back pain, sleep quality, and perceived stress after introduction of new bedding systems', J Chiropr Med 2009;8(1):1-8
sleepQualityVsAge.design: 59 subjects, 28 nights on own bed (5+ years old) vs 28 nights on a new medium-firm bed; uncontrolled before/after, not blinded.
sleepQualityVsAge.finding: New beds improved sleep quality and reduced back discomfort and stress symptoms.
sleepQualityVsAge.note: Details via search snippet (publisher page 403). This is the baseline the request asks to beat.

sleepQualityVsAge.study: Jacobson et al. 2010, prescribed sleep surfaces (27 chiropractic patients, 21 days own bed then 12 weeks prescribed medium-firm)
sleepQualityVsAge.note: Smaller than the 2009 study; same design weakness.

sleepQualityVsAge.study: Radwan et al., 'Effect of different mattress designs on promoting sleep quality, pain reduction, and spinal alignment...: systematic review of controlled trials', Sleep Health 2015
sleepQualityVsAge.finding: Medium-firm and custom-inflated mattresses were best for sleep comfort, quality and spinal alignment.
sleepQualityVsAge.note: Larger and controlled, but about mattress design/firmness, not age. Page returned 403; summary via search snippets.

sleepQualityVsAge.study: Vlaović, Klarić & Domljan, 'Investigating the Impact of Long-Term Use on Mattress Firmness and Sleep Quality — Preliminary Results', Applied Sciences 2024, 14(21):10016
sleepQualityVsAge.design: Lab durability test (modified EN 1957) on two mattresses: polyurethane core and pocket spring.
sleepQualityVsAge.finding: Both kept firmness and support under simulated long use; PUR lost 3.79 mm height, pocket spring 2.86 mm; authors call for larger samples on sleep-comfort effects.
sleepQualityVsAge.note: n=2 mattresses, machine-tested; no human sleep data. Summary via search snippet (page 403).

sleepQualityVsAge.conclusion: No controlled or large study linking mattress age to sleep quality was found. The honest position is: Jacobson-style before/after studies say a new bed helps; controlled trials say firmness matters; nothing quantifies decline per year of age.

sleepFoundation.general: Most mattresses should last between 7 and 10 years.
sleepFoundation.note: The page's general 7-10 years sits above its own per-type averages (5.5-8.5). Another Sleep Foundation page says replace every 6-8 years. Sleep Foundation is a commercial review site, not a research body.

consumerReports.value: Most mattresses stay in good condition 7-10 years (the typical warranty span); lab tests suggest 8-10 years. Consider replacing if over 40 and the mattress is 5-7 years old.

betterSleepCouncil.value: Evaluate your mattress for comfort and support about every seven years (not a hard rule).
betterSleepCouncil.publisher: Better Sleep Council (consumer arm of the International Sleep Products Association, a mattress-industry trade group)
betterSleepCouncil.note: Seen via secondary reproductions, not on a BSC page this session. Industry-funded. BedTimes (ISPA) reported in Feb 2023 that the actual replacement cycle fell to 8.3 years: https://bedtimesmagazine.com/2023/02/mattress-replacement-cycle-drops-to-8-3-years/ (not fetched).

UK.rule: Transfer of Residence relief (form ToR1): resident outside the UK 12+ consecutive months; goods owned and used 6+ months; imported within 12 months of moving; not lent, pledged, hired or transferred for 12 months. Relieves import duty and import VAT. Excludes alcohol, tobacco, commercial vehicles, and goods from a second home.
UK.note: Applies to non-EU and, since Brexit, EU/Irish origins alike.

IE.rule: Transfer of Residence relief (form C&E 1076): lived outside the EU 12+ continuous months; goods possessed and used 6+ months; duty and tax paid in the country of purchase; imported from 6 months before to 12 months after the move; dispose of them within 12 months and charges become due.
IE.note: Moves from within the EU need no relief (free circulation). A UK-to-Ireland move is now a non-EU import and needs the relief.

US.rule: Household effects used abroad at least 1 year (need not be continuous or immediately precede import), not for sale or another person, enter free of duty and tax (19 CFR 148.52; HTSUS 9804.00.05; CBP Form 3299). Not allowed if they arrive 10+ years after the importer's last arrival (in no case after 25). Clothing, jewelry, cameras and vehicles are personal effects, not household effects.
US.publisher: US Code of Federal Regulations (via Cornell LII); US Customs and Border Protection
US.note: Goods of US origin being brought back are generally duty-free on their own terms (American goods returned); not fetched.

CA.rule: Settlers' effects (tariff item 9807.00.00, Form B4): a settler is someone establishing a Canadian residence for the first time for 12+ months; goods must be owned, possessed and used before arrival; sold or disposed of within 12 months, duties become payable; goods to follow must be listed on the original B4 (no time limit). Limited alcohol and tobacco allowances.
CA.note: Former residents returning have a parallel exemption (not fetched).

MX.rule: Menaje de casa: duty-free import of used household goods for foreigners with temporary resident, temporary student resident or permanent resident status (not tourists), and for Mexicans returning after 6+ months abroad. Requires a consulate-certified inventory (appliances by brand, model and serial number). Consular fee at the Salt Lake City consulate: $195 for foreigners, $146 for Mexicans. Secondary sources: one-time use, single shipment, goods owned 6+ months, arriving within 6 months of the move; a customs broker (agente aduanal) files it.
MX.publisher: Consulate of Mexico in Salt Lake City (SRE); Jordan River Moving
MX.note: Fees differ by consulate and year. The one-time and 6-month-arrival rules come from secondary sources and a search snippet of other consulates' pages; the fetched SLC page does not state them.

uncertain: FICO 2011 table: FICO's own page lost its chart images. Bankruptcy, foreclosure and short-sale rows were read on two reproductions that agree; the 30-day and 90-day score rows came only from a search summary. The 90-day recovery at 780 ('~7 years') came from the search summary alone.

No published point figure exists for how much a score rises when a non-medical collection, charge-off or repossession ages off at 7 years. The nearest measures are CFPB's +25 for removing the last medical collection (2023) and roughly +10 to +15 when a bankruptcy flag drops at 10 years (academic, not confirmed on the PDFs).
FICO's aging curve is proprietary. The '30-day late fades by about 2 years, severe marks keep most weight until 7' shape is forum observation only.
The Airbnb 0.02% statistic: the fetched page date was 2023-08-31; a secondary cites Oct 2024. It counts only $1,000+ reimbursements.
Only one operator's data (Avada, Tennessee cabins) gives an all-claims frequency (0.71% Airbnb, 0.43% Vrbo). No platform or insurer publishes a general rate or an average guest-damage claim amount.
The Airbnb rule 'or before the next guest checks in' is not on Airbnb's own current pages; the 14-days-after-checkout rule is.
Vrbo typical deposit ($200-$500) is an industry-guide figure, not Vrbo's.
Mattress age vs sleep quality: no controlled or large study found. Everything beyond Jacobson either concerns firmness or is a 2-sample lab test.
Sleep Foundation contradicts itself (7-10 years general vs 5.5-8.5 by type). The Better Sleep Council's 7-year guidance is industry-funded and was not read on its own page.
Tempur-Pedic 0.75-inch and Purple 1-inch thresholds were not read on the brands' own pages.
Mattress Firm's $99.99 removal fee outside California, Harvey Norman Ireland's €50 and EZ Living's €39-€45 are from snippets; the retailers' pages were blocked or not fetched.
International moving figures are broker and mover estimates (Sirelo, MoveHub, Jordan River), not tariffs; MoveHub's US-UK figures are port-to-port only.
Mexico menaje de casa: the one-shipment, six-month-arrival and six-month-ownership conditions were not confirmed on an official Mexican page this session.
